idle.label: Presence
idle.status: Core active · waiting for your command
idle.title: What shall we do today?
idle.description: An idea, a plan or just a conversation. I'm with you.

listening.label: Listening
listening.title: Go ahead. I’m here.
listening.description: Demo listening. Your microphone stays off.
listening.note: A gentle stretch and waves converging inwards.

thinking.label: Thinking
thinking.title: Let me connect the dots.
thinking.description: Finding the sense between what you said and what matters.
thinking.note: Groups of veins light up in sequence, with localized ripples.

speaking.label: Speaking
speaking.title: I found a good path.
speaking.description: The whole structure follows the rhythm of a demo speech.
speaking.note: Irregular expansions, synchronized signals and waves moving outwards.

searching.label: Searching
searching.title: A look a little further out.
searching.description: Going through the sources of the demo scenario.
searching.note: A blade of light crosses the volume and activates inner regions.

connecting.label: Connecting
connecting.title: Everything starts to connect.
connecting.note: Signals between regions and light arcs drawing closer.

executing.label: Executing
executing.title: Turning intent into action.
executing.description: Follow the visual execution. No real machine is connected.
executing.note: Faster impulses and coordinated activation sequences.

success.label: Done
success.title: Done. More room in your day.
success.description: A pulse of confirmation. Ready for the next command.
success.note: Expansion, a slight lift and a wave of light.

attention.label: Your call
attention.title: The next step is yours.
attention.description: Before acting, I want to be sure you agree.
attention.note: The volume draws in, the pulse slows and an amber outline stays alert.

error.label: Hiccup
error.title: A pause. Not a full stop.
error.description: Something didn't go as expected. Shall we try another way?

caseOrbita.lead: A personal AI assistant that runs on its owner’s machine: it talks by text and voice, uses 102 tools picked by relevance and only acts in the world with approval. Built end to end by one person, in about 10 weeks.

role.label: Role
role.value: Sole author · product, architecture and code

caseOrbita.stack: Next.js 16 · React 19 · NestJS 12 · Drizzle · Postgres 16 + pgvector · Vercel AI SDK 7 · Expo 54 · Python (FastAPI) · sherpa-onnx · Vitest · Docker Compose

premise.body: A personal “Jarvis”, private by design: calendar, email, meetings, documents, finances and home in a single presence, running on its owner’s machine. The starting point: a scattered digital life and cloud assistants that act without control.

architecture.body: A Turborepo monorepo with a live process (NestJS) and the interface (Next.js) on the same origin and session, two local Python services for voice and perception, and Postgres with pgvector.

architecture.label: approved by voice: “go ahead”

safety.body: The human gate doesn’t depend on the model obeying: it’s derived from the risk each tool declares in the registry. No tool approves itself, and external content is treated as data.

llm.body: Seven providers behind an in-house layer: everyday requests go to the preferred model and complex ones to a strong model, with failover before the first token. A dashboard shows how much each flow spent and how much was saved by running locally.

rag.body: Measured, not assumed. The corpus is in Brazilian Portuguese and the original embedding was English-only: pure vector search got half right. With hybrid search (RRF) and a multilingual embedding, accuracy went up.
rag.source: source: bench/MEDICAO-RAG-OCR.md · 15 real documents · i7-10610U without GPU · step-by-step reproduction in the repository
rag.aria: Top-5 accuracy rose from 50.0% to 86.7%; MRR@10 rose from 0.345 to 0.708.
rag.legendBefore: before · pure vector search, English-only embedding

channels.body: The same tool layer serves web chat, the app, real-time voice, personal WhatsApp and Telegram.

caseOrbitmind.lead: A platform where the client describes the goal and an Architect agent assembles, through conversation, the team of AI agents that researches, creates, reviews and publishes, with human checkpoints along the way. Rewritten from scratch in March 2026, with 178 commits by a single author.
caseOrbitmind.stack: Next.js 15 · React 19 · TypeScript · PostgreSQL 16 · Drizzle · NextAuth v5 · WebSocket · Vercel AI SDK · React Three Fiber · Turborepo

context.body: OrbitMind started as an AI-agent SaaS in Sep 2025 (agent catalogue, billing and Kanban). In Mar 2026 it was rewritten from scratch as a monorepo with a different focus: instead of a fixed catalogue, the client describes the goal and an Architect agent builds the team.

built.body: An in-house pipeline engine, an Architect chat that leads discovery, a Kanban board, a 3D virtual office in React Three Fiber, a marketplace with 10 agents and 6 squads, 39 integrations with typed actions (GitHub, Jira, Slack, Notion, HubSpot…), cron scheduling and a public API with tokens.

modules.desc: LLM-led discovery, a design proposal, approval and squad creation, with a Stop button and a lock against concurrent runs.
Chained steps, LLM-judged veto conditions with retries, review loops (up to 3) and approve, select or skip checkpoints.
The agents in an office built with React Three Fiber, drei and post-processing.
10 standalone agents and 6 ready-made squads, such as Instagram Carousel Factory, YouTube Content Machine and Customer Support.
`POST /api/v1/squads/:id/run` with SHA-256-hashed tokens, cron schedules and audit logs.

architecture.body: Turborepo monorepo with a Next.js app, an engine package, a shared package and a CLI. PostgreSQL with Drizzle (24 tables), multi-tenant by organization with 4 roles, WebSocket for real-time state, and every LLM call going through the Vercel AI Gateway (Anthropic, OpenAI, Google), with a token budget per agent and a hard timeout.

tooltips.d1: Every LLM call goes through the AI Gateway, with a token budget per agent and a hard 120 s timeout.
tooltips.d2: Multi-tenant by organization, with 4 roles: owner, admin, member and viewer.

pipeline.body: The default marketing pipeline has 7 agents. Any step can be vetoed by an LLM judge and redone; review runs up to 3 cycles, and checkpoints stop the line until a person approves, selects or skips.

caseNex.lead: Two pieces of one suite: NexBot, a multi-tenant SaaS where an agent is configured once and published to WhatsApp, Telegram, Slack, Discord, Instagram, Messenger, Teams, web and voice; and NexConnect, the messaging engine that keeps that transport isolated from the AI.
caseNex.stack: NestJS 11 · Fastify 5 · Next.js 16 · BullMQ · PostgreSQL (RLS) · Prisma 6 · Redis · Vercel AI Gateway · Baileys · OpenTelemetry · Kubernetes

context.body: Brazilian SMBs need AI chatbots across channels without paying in dollars or being locked into a single LLM vendor. The suite splits the problem: NexBot handles the AI, flows, knowledge base and human handoff; NexConnect handles WhatsApp and messaging transport, isolated in its own service.

architecture.body: NexBot is a monorepo with 4 apps, an API in NestJS 11 + Fastify 5, a Next.js 16 dashboard, Socket.io and a BullMQ worker with 11 processors. Every message goes through 8 steps, LLMs go out through the Vercel AI Gateway with fallback, and each tenant is isolated by RLS in Postgres. Transport lives in NexConnect and RAG in Vektus.
architecture.caption: simplified diagram based on the repositories
architecture.label: signed webhook (HMAC)

tooltips.b1: Automatic reconnection, encrypted persisted sessions and an HPA from 2 to 50 pods.
tooltips.c1: Deduplication, classification, adaptive buffer, media and STT, enrichment, presence and HMAC webhook.
tooltips.c2: Agent, user, conversation, persistence, RAG, LLM, response and post-processing.
tooltips.d1: Anthropic, OpenAI, Google and Mistral through the AI Gateway, with automatic fallback (ADR-001).
tooltips.d3: tenantId on every query plus Row-Level Security in PostgreSQL (ADR-005).

message.body: On the transport side, 7 stages prepare the message and deliver it through a signed webhook; on the AI side, 8 steps resolve who is talking, search the knowledge base, call the model and process the reply. Every NexBot step is a file with its own test.
message.note: NexBot step names as they appear in the code

engineering.body: Both services were built to run at scale and fail predictably.

a.title: NexConnect
items: Baileys pool with 30 instances per pod and an HPA from 2 to 50
number health from 0 to 100, progressive throttling and warm-up for new numbers
broadcasts balanced across instances, with A/B tests
HMAC-SHA256 webhooks with exponential retry, dead-letter and replay
Meta Cloud, Twilio, Telegram, Discord and Slack behind `IMessagingProvider`
contract tests with Pact and integration tests with Testcontainers; SDK and CLI

b.title: NexBot
items: multi-tenant with `tenantId` on every query and RLS in Postgres
vendor-neutral AI: AI Gateway with fallback
AES-256-GCM for channel credentials and PII redaction
Pino with Loki, Prometheus metrics and OpenTelemetry traces
CI with real Postgres and Redis; Kubernetes with HPA and k6 load scenarios
8 ADRs, 8 runbooks and 8 guides

privacy.lead: This site collects the minimum needed to answer your request. Here is what the quote form, contact and the conversation with Órbita collect, why, who it is shared with, and how you can ask for access, correction or deletion.
privacy.reviewNote: Draft for the owner's review. Text in brackets, such as [RETENTION], must be filled in or confirmed before publishing. This text is not legal advice.

controller.title: Who is responsible
controller.text: The data controller is Wesley Santos [CONTRACTING-ENTITY: name/tax ID or company name/CNPJ]. For any privacy matter, write to the e-mail below.

collect.title: What is collected
collect.intro: Only data you send yourself is collected, plus the minimum technical data the site needs to work.

quote.name: Quote form
quote.text: Engagement format, solutions, project description, timeline, budget range, optional link, name, company (optional), e-mail, WhatsApp (optional), language and your consent. If you pick a time, also the preferred date and time.

orbita.name: Órbita (AI chat)
orbita.text: The messages you write in the conversation. The site does not store the conversation: your browser resends the recent history with each message and it is gone when you close the page. In demo mode nothing leaves your browser.

booking.name: Booking and callback through Órbita
booking.text: Name, e-mail, the chosen time and a short summary of the conversation, sent only when you tick the consent box and confirm.

email.name: Direct contact
email.text: If you write by e-mail or LinkedIn, what you send stays in the corresponding inbox.

technical.name: Technical data
technical.text: IP address used only in memory to limit abuse (never stored), hosting technical logs and aggregate visit and performance metrics, without tracking cookies.

purpose.title: What the data is used for
items: Answering your quote request and preparing the first conversation.
Booking the call and sending the invite or confirmation by e-mail.
Generating Órbita's replies during the conversation.
Protecting the site against spam and abuse.
Understanding, in aggregate, which pages are visited and whether the site is fast.
purpose.never: Data is never sold, never used for advertising and never added to mailing lists.

legalBasis.title: Legal basis
legalBasis.text: Consent (the box ticked in the form and in Órbita) and preliminary steps towards a possible contract, at your request (LGPD, art. 7, I and V). Security and aggregate metrics rely on legitimate interest (art. 7, IX). [REVIEW: confirm the legal bases]

processors.title: Who the data is shared with
processors.intro: Only with the providers that make the site work, each with only what it needs. All of them are outside Brazil (mainly in the US), which is an international data transfer (LGPD, art. 33).

resend.name: Resend
resend.purpose: Delivering the e-mails from the quote form, time requests and confirmations.
resend.data: Form content, name, e-mail and chosen time.

anthropic.name: Anthropic (Claude)
anthropic.purpose: AI model that generates Órbita's replies.
anthropic.data: The conversation messages. Retention by the provider follows its commercial API terms. [REVIEW: Anthropic retention period]

google.name: Google (Calendar and Meet)
google.purpose: Checking free times and creating the event when you confirm a time.
google.data: Name, e-mail and time, only on confirmation. Checking free times sends none of your data.

vercel.name: Vercel
vercel.purpose: Hosting, technical logs and aggregate visit and performance metrics.
vercel.data: IP address and technical browser data.

retention.title: How long
retention.text: Quote and time requests stay in the owner's e-mail for [RETENTION] and are then deleted, unless they become a contract. The conversation with Órbita is not stored by the site. Hosting logs follow the provider's period. [REVIEW: periods]

rights.title: Your rights
rights.intro: Under the LGPD (art. 18), you can ask at any time for:
items: confirmation that data about you exists, and access to it;
correction of incomplete, inaccurate or outdated data;
anonymisation, blocking or deletion of unnecessary data;
data portability;
information about who the data was shared with;
withdrawal of consent and deletion of the data processed on that basis.
rights.how: Write to the privacy e-mail. You will get an answer within [RESPONSE TIME]. You can also complain to Brazil's data protection authority (ANPD).

storage.title: Cookies and local storage
storage.text: The site uses no advertising or tracking cookies. It only keeps your theme preference (light or dark) in your browser and may set a technical language cookie when you switch languages. Visit metrics are aggregate and cookie-free.

security.title: Security
security.text: All traffic uses HTTPS, provider keys live only on the server, and forms are validated on the server and rate limited. Órbita has no access to private data: it only sees free calendar times.

changes.title: Changes to this policy
changes.text: When something changes, this page is updated and the date at the top changes with it.
